idea: Basic plumbing maintenance every homeowner should know
title: Maintaining Under-Sink Angle Stop Shutoff Valves
description:
In a fixture emergency, the under-sink shutoff valve—commonly called an angle stop—is your primary defense against water damage. However, when left untouched for years, mineral deposits dissolved in water can build up around the valve stem and seat, causing the valve to seize or leak around the packing nut when forced open or closed.

Exercising your shutoff valves twice a year keeps internal parts moving freely and helps prevent mineral scale from locking the mechanism. If you notice stiff movement or minor weeping around old multi-turn gate-style valves, upgrading to a quarter-turn brass ball valve provides a far more reliable seal.

How recently have you checked or operated your under-sink shutoff valves?

on_image_text.hook: Test Your Shutoff Valves Before an Emergency
on_image_text.explanation: Unused shutoff valves accumulate mineral scale over time, causing internal valve stems to seize when forced.
on_image_text.takeaway: Gently operate shutoff valves twice a year to maintain mechanical movement and prevent mineral buildup.
